title: Tanzanian Tamarind Fish
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Samaki wa Ukwaju — fish marinated in tamarind and spices, pan-seared golden, finished in a tamarind-onion sauce. The sweet-sour-spiced fish dish of the Swahili coast.
longDesc: Tamarind and fish is one of the great Swahili coast flavour combinations — the tartness of tamarind perfectly counterpoints Indian Ocean fish. Found at every coastal food stall.
steps: Marinate fish in tamarind, garlic, turmeric, cumin, salt for 30 minutes.
Sear fish 3—4 minutes per side until golden. Remove.
Cook onions in same pan until golden.
Add tomatoes, tamarind, sugar. Cook 5 minutes.
Add water. Return fish. Simmer gently 5—8 minutes.
chefTips: Sear first — the crust is structural.
commonMistakes: Skipping the sear — fish breaks in sauce.
cookingScience: The initial sear creates a protein crust that structurally reinforces the fish fillet — allowing it to survive sauce simmering without breaking apart.
sustainabilityTips: Tamarind trees grow throughout coastal Tanzania.
culturalNote: Samaki wa Ukwaju is the taste of the Swahili coast — the tamarind that arrived on Arab dhows paired with Indian Ocean fish that was always here.
